common_name: Silky Deep Red Milkweed (Crimson-Flowered Tropical Milkweed)

planting.note: Start seeds indoors 4-6 weeks before last frost or direct sow after all frost danger passes; in zones 8-11 cut plants back hard in late fall or winter to interrupt continuous bloom and reduce OE parasite buildup on evergreen foliage.

directions: Silky Deep Red is a dwarf-statured selection of tropical milkweed bred for its richly saturated crimson-red flowers ringed with contrasting golden-yellow hoods, held above the plant in tidy, upright umbels from late spring through frost. Sow seed in a warm, sunny site with fertile, well-drained soil; plants flower reliably in their first season and stay more compact than the straight species, making them well suited to containers and small-space pollinator gardens. Like all tropical milkweed, it serves as both a nectar source and monarch caterpillar host plant, but growers in zones 8-11 should cut plants back hard in late fall or winter to interrupt continuous blooming and reduce the buildup of the OE parasite that can accumulate on evergreen tropical milkweed foliage. Treat as a reseeding warm-season annual outside its hardiness range, since it will not survive a hard freeze.

directions: Silky Gold is a clear golden-yellow flowered selection of tropical milkweed, lacking the red-orange tones of the species and standard cultivars, producing flat-topped umbels of buttery yellow blooms continuously from late spring until frost. Start seed indoors in a warm location or direct sow once the soil has warmed, since seedlings are frost-tender and grow quickly as temperatures rise; container-grown transplants often flower within weeks of being set out. The uniform yellow color makes it a popular choice for gardeners wanting a monarch host plant that reads as a distinct color note rather than blending into more common orange-and-red tropical milkweed plantings. As with other Asclepias curassavica selections, cut plants back in late fall in frost-free zones to help interrupt monarch overwintering behavior and reduce OE parasite loads on the foliage.
